issues.what: the palette is almost all mid-grey: grey sky, grey fog, grey stone, grey sea. There is no bright accent, no deep black, and no warm or cool contrast, so at phone size the first frame reads as a dull, overcast still and gives a scrolling thumb little reason to stop
issues.fix: add one strong value or colour accent from frame 1, such as a break of light catching the tips of the spires or a darker sea against brighter fog, so the silhouette separates hard from the sky

issues.what: almost nothing changes across the ten frames except a slow drift closer and slightly upward, and the fog thins a little. No event, reveal or motion arrives that rewards staying, and the shot only grows marginally
issues.fix: put a clear change inside the opening: fog parting to reveal the base or more spires, a shaft of light sweeping across, a wave breaking, or a faster, more decisive push toward the arch

issues.what: this is a wide 16:9 frame with the subject in the left half and empty grey fog and sky to the right. In a vertical phone feed it would be shown small, and the curved spires become a small, low-contrast shape, so it is not immediately clear what they are (rock, horns, ruins or ships)
issues.fix: frame tighter on the arch so it fills the frame, or compose for vertical with the spires centred and filling the height

issues.where: the fog bank behind the sea line, from the left spire to the right edge
issues.what: the fog sits as a flat, even band with a straight top edge, and it cuts the spires off at the base. It looks like a layer laid over the image rather than mist moving around the forms, and it flattens the depth
issues.fix: break up the fog's top edge and density, let wisps wrap around the spires, and let some of the base show through

issues.where: the smaller background spires between the two main arms
issues.what: the thin spires behind the main pair are so faint and low-contrast that they barely read, even on a paused frame, and they add clutter rather than scale
issues.fix: either give them atmospheric separation so they read clearly as distant forms, or remove them
